transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. I want to use part of today's weekly operating review to address the escalation handoff issues we've been seeing. Lina and Omar, you both currently share responsibility for handing client escalations from Client Operations to Implementation, and several recent handoffs have led to disagreement about who communicates with the client and who owns the internal follow-up. With a major client rollout starting in four weeks, we need a stable handoff process in place well before then. I'd like to hear from both of you on where the friction is happening, and then I'll make a decision on restructuring the responsibility and updating our coordination process so we're not leaving this ambiguous going forward.

transcript.text: Happy to share what I've been seeing. The main breakdowns have been on three fronts. First, on client-facing communication: since the six-week agreement expired and was never documented, there have been escalations where both Omar and I reached out to the client independently, which created mixed messages and understandably frustrated the clients involved. Second, on internal follow-up: there have been cases where each of us assumed the other was driving the root-cause investigation, so things stalled with no clear owner. And third, on handoff timing itself: without a documented process, the point at which an escalation officially moves from Client Operations to Implementation has been inconsistent — sometimes it happens too early, before we've gathered enough context, and sometimes too late, which delays the Implementation team's response. I think restoring the split that worked during those six weeks — me on client-facing communication, Omar on internal root-cause follow-up — but actually documenting it this time would resolve most of this. But I want to hear Omar's constraint and request before we finalize anything, since those clearly could affect how we structure the coordination.
